title: Nuij's theorem invoked in unproved univariate '$k\ge\deg$ ⇒ simple roots' form (load-bearing for simple-root reduction)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Lemma "simple"(i) in solution.tex: *"(i) is Nuij's theorem [Nuij]: ... after at least $m$ applications all roots become simple, so $(1-\epsilon\,d/dx)^k f$ is monic real-rooted with simple roots for every $k\ge m$."*

**Issue.** The whole simple-root reduction (and hence every smoothness/Hessian/contraction assertion downstream) rests on the claim

> for a monic real-rooted $f$ of degree $m$ and every $\epsilon>0$, $(1-\epsilon\,d/dx)^k f$ is monic real-rooted with **simple** roots whenever $k\ge m$.

This precise **univariate** statement is asserted as "Nuij's theorem" but Nuij (1968, *A note on hyperbolic polynomials*, Math. Scand. 23) is about **multivariate homogeneous hyperbolic polynomials** and the deformation $(1+\epsilon\langle e,\nabla\rangle)$ landing in the interior of the hyperbolicity cone. The univariate "$k\ge\deg f \Rightarrow$ simple roots" form is not literally that theorem and is used without proof.

**Why it is genuinely load-bearing and non-trivial.**
- One application is provably NOT enough: $(1-\epsilon D)(x-c)^3$ retains a double root at $c$ for every $\epsilon$ (verified numerically). So simplicity really requires several applications, and the threshold "$k\ge\deg$" is the content.
- The solution uses exactly $k=n$ on the inputs ($T_\epsilon p$, $T_\epsilon q$) and $k=2n$ on the convolution ($T_\epsilon^2(p\boxplus_n q)$), i.e. it sits at/above the threshold — but the threshold itself is unproved.

**Supporting numerics.** The discriminant of $(1-\epsilon D)^m x^m$ is nonzero for $m\le 7$ (symbolic computation), confirming the extremal $m$-fold-root case becomes simple after exactly $m$ applications, so "$k\ge m$" is the right bar.

**What must be supplied.** Either a correct citation for the univariate statement, or a self-contained proof. Suggested route: $1-\epsilon\,d/dx$ preserves real-rootedness because $1-\epsilon t$ has only real zeros (Hermite–Poulain / Pólya–Schur theory of real-stability-preserving operators); then an induction / Rolle-interlacing multiplicity-reduction argument shows $m$ applications suffice for degree $m$. The extremal single-$m$-fold-root case is handled by the discriminant computation above.
